rows.text: # Probe model materialization — freeze review

2026-09-07. **CONCRETE BYTES ACCEPTED AND FROZEN.**
User acceptance closes PROBE-MODEL-BYTE-A as a materialization PASS and authorizes probe runtime
implementation under this model only. PROBE-A..P remain unpassed. The 15-file regeneration proof
records pre-freeze review metadata; acceptance updates report status only, not the seven artifacts.

[Review manifest](campaign2-probe-model/REVIEW_MANIFEST.json) contains all seven canonical byte
artifacts and readable counterparts, exact versions, semantic dependency bundle, fixed whole-profile
bindings, old-vs-probe structural diff and SHA256 preservation hashes for 30 old .1/.2 files.

ModelIdentity SHA256:
`2cc10295fc9c8f8b0777fc0ac56c526bcc4f4d26ec865bcad3776d696d5bf454`.

ContentManifest/Identity and ParameterManifest/Identity are byte-identical. Registry position 0
adds five descriptors, three governed union entries and one definition; position 5 adds eleven
roles. Positions 1..4 are byte-identical. ModelIdentity changes only fields 1 (RulesVersion) and
6 (RegistryIdentity, including changed RegistrySchemaVersion). Numeric/RNG versions are unchanged.

The review-only compiler validates the exact first specimen with its four committed boolean
variants, checks inherited declarations through the unchanged bounded compiler, and returns model
commitments only. It neither installs profile handlers nor constructs a run. The existing public
factory remains unchanged and does not activate this probe RulesVersion. Registry equality is
canonical, preserving set permutation equivalence; absent/extra/wrong specimen declarations reject.

Verification: production build and reference boundary check PASS; 72 test files / 459 tests PASS.
Three new packaging tests cover shifted layout, missing governed union entries, mixed profiles,
four distinct permission models and canonical permutation identity. All 15 generated packet files
were deleted from the verified probe-only directory, regenerated in a fresh process, compared by
SHA256 and verified in another fresh process. [Rematerialization proof](CAMPAIGN2_PROBE_REMATERIALIZATION_PROOF.json).
All 30 prior model files retain their recorded hashes. This is materialization evidence, not
authoritative runtime or full PROBE-PACK qualification.

Concrete model freeze is accepted. Runtime implementation may proceed; PROBE-A..P, ADAPT-9b,
parent control 9 and PHEN-ADAPT remain open. Subsequent implementation gaps must be resolved
explicitly without silently changing these frozen bytes.
# Diagnostic probe — model/profile packaging revision 1

2026-09-07. **SHAPE ACCEPTED**, with canonical-position and whole-profile clarifications below.
Model materialization is authorized; authoritative probe runtime remains blocked until model-byte
freeze. [Materialized review packet](campaign2-probe-model/REVIEW_MANIFEST.json).
Depends on accepted regulatory-diagnostic-probe/0.1-candidate and frozen
regulatory-probe-allocation/0.1-candidate. This document proposes executable profile bindings;
it does not change probe mathematics, identity allocation, SEM/EVID or the bounded .2 model.
## Inspection and selected boundary

`src/campaign2/modelPackaging.ts` selects an exact RulesVersion bundle and checks a closed
registry-kind inventory plus exact union entries. `factory.ts` selects the ordered-input,
persistence and trace adapters internally. Existing compilers do not admit probe records or
sources. Appending probe data while retaining those profile versions would misstate their
accepted language. The new profile must be explicitly selected from its RulesVersion, never
inferred from input shape, a caller callback or fallback to the old bounded implementation.
## Proposed exact version binding

| Surface | Proposed binding |
|---|---|
| RulesVersion | rules/campaign2-regulatory-probe/0.1-candidate |
| RegistrySchemaVersion | campaign2-probe-registry/0.1-candidate |
| Ordered input profile | campaign2-probe-ordered-input/0.1-candidate |
| Trace profile | campaign2-probe-trace-binding/0.1-candidate |
| Persistence profile | campaign2-probe-persistence/0.1-candidate |
| ContentSchemaVersion | existing content/0.2-candidate |
| ParameterSchemaVersion | existing campaign2-parameters/0.1-candidate |
| NumericProfileVersion | existing numeric/exact-1 |
| RandomAlgorithmVersion | exact existing bounded .2 value |

The compatibility bundle retains the exact ordered entries in
`docs/formal/CAMPAIGN2_BOUNDED_RULES_02.md`, then appends
regulatory-diagnostic-probe/0.1-candidate and campaign2-probe-trace-binding/0.1-candidate.
Retaining campaign2-trace-binding/0.1-candidate names the unchanged fixed-pulse/EVID/ADAPT
submapping, not permission to dispatch the old whole-model trace compiler on a probe model.
The new profile owns the composed dispatcher. No alternative scalar, padding or route policies.
Budget/event topology changes require accepted RulesVersion changes, never host switches.
## Exact first model and six-slot registry delta

Use the frozen .2 model as the preserved base for declaration reuse. The new model keeps its
content, REG anchor/domain, five adaptation rules, state families/owners, fixed-pulse channels,
parameters, numeric and random artifacts byte-identical where unchanged. Do not overwrite any
old artifact. The new model's registry and RulesVersion differ; its RegistrySchemaVersion differs
as explicitly proposed above. No claim that only one ModelIdentity field changes.

| Registry slot | Proposed contents relative to frozen .2 |
|---|---|
| 0: schema descriptors and RegistryEntry set | Retain all prior entries; add descriptors 331..335, the three exact type-259 entries [335,1..3], and one probe definition entry. |
| 1: phase registry | Byte-identical ordering-phases/2-candidate; no new phase. |
| 2: mutation authorities | Byte-identical; probe has NoStateWrites. |
| 3: read-only family declarations | Byte-identical empty set; no roster/cognitive family. |
| 4: state-key grammar declarations | Byte-identical; existing RegulatoryAdaptationKey/294 reused. |
| 5: identity roles | Retain prior rows; add the eleven exact allocated role rows for 331..335. No role for record-valued 335/4. |

The one added RegistryEntry uses stable definition/regulatory-diagnostic-probe, kind
registry/regulatory-diagnostic-probe, accepted probe version and record 331. Its C and V are the
existing qualified fixture character and regulatory variable. Available=true; ObserverPermitted=true.
Its embedded 332 uses existing observer/bridge-subject, SubjectId=C, model-authored
channel/regulatory-diagnostic-probe in namespace 1005, model-authored
modality/diagnostic-regulatory-probe in namespace 1006, and the frozen unit member
unit/diagnostic-regulatory-level in namespace 1039. Channel identity must differ from the fixed
pulse channel. These model-authored values are concrete fixture choices, not new identity families.

Permission/availability controls change only their explicit definition booleans and therefore
derive separate ModelIdentities. Each exposure-count A/B pair uses the same complete model.
The read path is compiled from the committed 331 C/V by the accepted fixed consumer; it is not
a new freely authored read declaration, state family or configurable function. Union entries
are validated and committed before any carrier codec is available; exact missing/extra/changed
rows reject. The old profile retains its old closed union inventory unchanged.
## Ordered-input and source authority

Reuse the five-position canonical list envelope, not a new record allocation. The new profile
admits exactly the existing authored-adaptation source plus event/regulatory-diagnostic-probe
with record 333. Both are InputOnly under original compiler authority, not public scheduling.
Probe DueAt > initial clock, Phase=110, dependencies/parents empty, at most one probe per instant,
and no adaptation source at that instant. ProbeDefinitionId resolves exactly to the committed
singleton definition. No initial generated probe stage, padding event or EVID event is admitted.

The entire original manifest determines initial source IDs/sequences and RunIdentity. Equal
probe opportunity bytes are used in both counterfactual runs. Example corpus setup: original
exposure at T0=2 with counts 0/1, identical probe at T1=4; R0=50, Scale=10, both effective values
valid. Fixed-pulse observation at T0 stays equal, retained D differs after 140, and the first
observer-accessible difference is the probe's 203. X/E/L remain equal. This is a proposed fixture,
not a run result or PHEN verdict. Later common sentinel controls retain the fixed-pulse source.
## Trace and observation validator closure

The composed trace dispatcher admits exactly the old fixed-pulse/source/SEM/EVID/ADAPT rows plus
the eight allocated probe kinds. Probe-owned rows use the accepted probe mapping, including
actual EventTypeId as RecordKind, exact D RegisteredReadDomain and conditional ActualReadRecords
at 110, no patch/diff, and no padding occurrence. Permitted E/L retain the actual EVID mapping.
The same kind cannot have competing handlers or trace owners. Intra-instant failure rolls back
all outputs, traces, child events and five ordinal advances.

The 203 validator admits the new transformation version only for the exact diagnostic producer
and committed channel: Point, equal reduced rational endpoints n/Scale, precision 1, empty tokens
and SafeSourceReferences. Truth and channel matching occurs on authenticated staged input before
publication. No generic effect compiler or generic 201 mode is widened. Archived observations
validate their canonical shape and committed diagnostic channel/version; historical n must not be
recomputed from current D. Actual producer/equality evidence belongs to the accepted trace/causal
closure, not a new observer-side truth pointer. EVID remains zero-read, unchanged 227→269→270.
## Persistence and materialization gate

Reuse accepted canonical save record/fields, exact boundary-only saves and ordinary allocator
continuation. No padding field, ticket, closure or new persistent character root. The new profile
adds allocated record/union and probe producer validation to the archived output/trace graph and
pending-source validator. Restore reconstructs original source authority by scratch compilation
of the complete manifest, requires exact pending InputOnly subset equality at B, and rejects
missing/extra/changed sources. It does not replay history or use a trace certificate. No pending
probe stage is legal in a successful boundary save. Wrong RulesVersion/profile or missing adapter
rejects before runtime construction; no migration alias to .2.

After packaging acceptance, materialize the new model in a separate artifact directory and record
all six canonical component hashes plus ModelIdentity bytes/digest, old-artifact preservation,
exact registry entry/role/union differences and decode/re-encode parity. No digest is invented
here. Existing artifact compilers require additive support before they can produce this model;
authoritative execution remains gated until commitment and explicit implementation authorization.

Review requested: exact version bundle, six-slot delta, original-source/trace/restore closure and
concrete model vocabulary. No further numeric allocation or diagnostic semantic redesign proposed.
## Acceptance clarifications and frozen packaging controls

The table uses canonical zero-based positions 0..5; earlier 1..6 labels were human ordinals only.
The accepted RulesVersion requires exactly the four new registry/input/persistence/trace profile
bindings in the version table. Retained semantic dependencies never select old whole profiles.
No old-parser fallback, try-bounded-then-probe, runtime extension or probe autodetection is allowed.
One new whole input profile owns both source grammars. One new whole trace profile owns every
event exactly once. One new persistence profile owns complete continuation, including probe output
and source validation. Fields 8/9/10 stay empty only because this closure has no runtime analytical
anchors, random consumers or continuing couplings. Padding adds none.

| Control | Frozen obligation | Current evidence |
|---|---|---|
| PROBE-PACK-A | Exact canonical positions 0..5; shifted/alternate layout rejects. | Review compiler negative control passes. |
| PROBE-PACK-B | Probe rules reject old input/persistence/whole trace; old .2 rejects probe bindings. | Review binding controls pass; authoritative selection remains gated. |
| PROBE-PACK-C | Old authored source uses the new whole input profile's explicit branch, no old-profile fallback. | FROZEN, NOT PASSED; input runtime not implemented. |
| PROBE-PACK-D | Exact descriptor/union/definition/role delta; invalid change rejects or admitted change alters identity. | Structural materialization and missing-union control pass; complete mutation coverage remains open. |
| PROBE-PACK-E | Either committed boolean changes registry and ModelIdentity. | All four review model digests distinct; canonical permutations equal. |
| PROBE-PACK-F | Archived diagnostic bytes never re-derived from current displacement. | FROZEN, NOT PASSED; probe restore not implemented. |
These component findings do not pass PROBE-A..P or any parent campaign gate.
# Probe .2 runtime qualification — pass 4

**Current verdict: PROBE-A..P QUALIFIED; ADAPT-9a PASS (user ruling 2026-09-07).**
Accessor A..E remain PASS. F retains F1/F2 split scope; G retains G1/G2/G3 bounded/generic
numeric scope. No temporal or broader signed-domain public model was executed. ADAPT-9b and
all parent campaign gates remain OPEN. Subsequent prose retains the qualification history.

Historical submission disposition: [assembled PROBE-A..P review packet](CAMPAIGN2_PROBE_QUALIFICATION_REVIEW.md)
is ready for qualification review. Its proposed whole-vector dispositions supersede the earlier
partial inventory for review purposes only; no whole-probe acceptance is presumed.

2026-09-07. Implementation: `regulatory-diagnostic-probe/0.1-candidate` with
`campaign2-probe-trace-binding/0.2-candidate`, exclusively under frozen
`rules/campaign2-regulatory-probe/0.2-candidate`. ModelDigest remains
`fda39ae4a8d82cbf531b41ce35c9af7ebb2ec5c7f233c4f7adbd7e6d7eba80e9`.

The user froze the seven-artifact successor packet and closed PROBE-ACCESSOR-MODEL-BYTE.
That disposition authorizes this implementation; the evidence below was executed afterward.
Probe .1 and all 45 earlier packet files remain preserved. No allocation or semantic shape changed.
## Implemented surface

The public data-only factory selects the exact successor compiler and probe-owned whole input,
trace and persistence profiles. InputOnly source authentication precedes probe execution. The
source reads only the registered D(C,V) leaf through ContractReadProjection and records the exact
permanent accessor; REG receives detached D for validation and supplies R0 at the same time.
Truth/334 stores signed n; dedicated channel/332 produces permitted observation/203 as exact
n/Scale. The production SEM reservation/freeze feeds the existing admitted EVID path.

Suppressed branches use private discarded ordinal advances and the fixed eight-event topology.
No probe state patch is produced. Restore includes probe schema, carrier, channel, lattice,
provenance and accessor validation; historical truth is not recomputed from current D. The
existing bounded model and its fixed-pulse source retain their original behavior.
## Executed evidence and limits

| Control | Current disposition and evidence |
|---|---|
| PROBE-ACCESSOR-A/B/C | PASS: real factory exact one/zero read cardinality; four wrong-member substitutions, including both ADAPT accessors, reject and roll back. |
| PROBE-ACCESSOR-D/E | PASS: executable identity comparison changes only field 1; manifests and fields 2..6 equal. Exact .2 binding succeeds, .1 identity fails, .1 public factory fails, old/other/latest profile strings fail support. |
| PROBE-A/D/H | Positive runtime witnesses: paired histories produce n=50/51 and q=5 and q=51/10, first permitted difference at 203, equal prior observer projections and equal matched X/E/L; four availability/permission variants have the required output counts. |
| PROBE-E/N | Allocator/output evidence: hidden-D pairs in each suppressed branch preserve complete permitted projection and later common sentinel; all four variants advance five runtime ordinals and seven child IDs/sequences. Full negative padding-inspection qualification remains open. |
| PROBE-F | PASS — SPLIT SCOPE. F1 executes temporal REG and the production probe consumer; F2 witnesses exact frozen-profile exclusion and unchanged specimen admission. User accepted both sublabels and their conjunction. |
| PROBE-I | Earlier 45 artifact files preserved; existing bounded later-challenge regression passes. |
| PROBE-K | All eight trace-failure slots in four branches, all probe-owned allocation failure sites, recovery, fresh-process continuation and archive output closure pass. See pass 3 for exact scope. |
| PROBE-L/M | Positive unchanged-state and equal-X/E/L evidence. Existing isolated EVID component retained. Full probe-specific forbidden dependency/scalar-propagation substitutions remain open. |
| PROBE-B/C/G/J/O/P | Partial or inherited component evidence only; do not infer complete vector PASS from the smoke/control suite. Further state-capability, numeric-domain, child/source forgery and fixed-policy adversarial coverage is required. |

Tests: `campaign2ProbeRuntime.test.ts` (15), `campaign2ProbeAccessorVersion.test.ts` (1),
`campaign2ProbeTemporalScope.test.ts` (1), with existing probe input and model-review suites.
Pass-1 regression was 74 files / 477 tests PASS. Pass-2 final full regression is
**80 files / 523 tests PASS**. Final production build, type checking and reference import
boundary also PASS. No preserved reference source was modified.

[Mutation proof](CAMPAIGN2_PROBE_RUNTIME_MUTATION_PROOF.json): 15-test baseline PASS and seven
production substitutions detected: ignore D, denominator 1, ignore availability, ignore permission,
skip padding advance, borrow truth namespace, borrow ADAPT accessor. Fingerprints name the exact
execution source and test. This is component evidence, not an exhaustive PROBE-A..P verdict.
Older campaign mutation reports retain their own historical fingerprints; this run does not
refresh or re-certify them after shared host/factory changes.
## PROBE-F accepted split scope

The frozen first specimen commits rate=0 and permits only the two availability/permission
booleans to vary. A time-varying REG registration is valid under accepted REG but is deliberately
rejected by this exact public model compiler. Broadening that compiler or silently assigning
changed declarations the frozen identity would contradict the accepted model packaging.

The executable component witness uses the real REG compiler and production probe execution,
with authored anchor=50, rate=1, TIME Scale=INT64_MAX and measurement Scale=10. At MAX-1 the
reference is 50; at MAX it is 51. Two reads at MAX with D=0 are byte-identical; D=1 gives n=52
and a distinct permitted scalar. State and declaration bytes stay unchanged. This exercises
source plus observation, not the full scheduler/SEM/EVID continuation. The same altered
declarations are rejected by the public frozen specimen; the original is accepted.

The user accepted PROBE-F1 (generic temporal positive) and PROBE-F2 (exact public exclusion),
with parent PROBE-F PASS iff both pass. Both pass in `campaign2ProbeTemporalScope.test.ts`.
The readout assertions also fix q=50/10, 51/10 and 52/10. Equal D across MAX-1 and MAX isolates
reference drift; it is not adaptation evidence. At matched MAX, changing only D by 1 changes n
by exactly 1 and q by exactly 1/Scale. No ModelIdentity comparison is made between the generic
fixture and frozen specimen. No full public-runtime time-varying model was executed or claimed.
A temporal public model is deferred until a phenomenon requires one; none is required for F.
## Qualification pass 2 — accepted F split and transactional expansion

`campaign2ProbeRollbackStages.test.ts` passes 32 cases: all eight event slots across all four
availability/permission variants. Injected trace failure follows each slot's work, covering truth
allocation, observation/reservation, SEM freeze, both EVID stages and discarded padding advances.
Every case verifies complete instant rollback and exact continuation from the pre-failure save
against a clean run. This does not yet substitute a failure inside the allocator call itself.

The capability audit found arithmetic still in the state-bearing host function. Corrected forward:
the host retains its exact registered read and actual-read trace; `probeReadout.ts` receives only
detached bigint reference/displacement operands through a null-prototype closed capability.
Ten substitutions requesting state, root, other C/V, roster, provider, entries, read, constructor
or prototype fail in the actual public runtime with no committed output. Public and temporal
positive witnesses still pass. This changes implementation isolation, not declarations or math.
The seven-mutant proof was refreshed against both host and detached arithmetic fingerprints.

`campaign2ProbeNumericDomain.test.ts` exercises accepted generic REG with signed [-100,100]
and Scale=10 through the production source and observation code: -100,-99,-1,0,1,99,100 map to
exact point rationals; -101 and 101 reject before occurrence allocation. State is unchanged.
The frozen public profile rejects the widened registration. This is the narrow broader-substrate
scope authorized by the user's continuation ruling, not a public negative-level model witness.

`campaign2ProbeChildAuthority.test.ts` rejects unassociated and altered payloads, event IDs,
sequences, times, phases, kinds, parents and dependencies; original children remain executable,
then replay/rebinding/closed-executor reuse rejects. Wrong definition cannot bind to the emission.

[Padding source audit](CAMPAIGN2_PROBE_PADDING_AUDIT.json) checks the exact fixed budget,
private zero-argument void consumer, discarded allocation result and statement-only call sites.
Six source substitutions (capture, return, compare, expose, changed count, allocator-derived budget)
reject. This is implementation qualification combined with the separate runtime budget/sentinel
witnesses; it is not a new runtime validator, registry or permission to revise profile policy.

[Fresh-process continuation](CAMPAIGN2_PROBE_CONTINUATION_PROOF.json) passes: an exposure
checkpoint is handed to a separate process using only source declarations, original inputs and
save. Probe plus later sentinel produce an identical complete 55,782-byte final save containing
26 trace records. Original initial state is not separately transferred. This closes the prior
fresh-process runtime continuation gap, without implying all of PROBE-K is passed.

New fixture-authoring failures were corrected without changing production semantics: SimInstant
requires bigint, interval field 3 is upper-presence (upper value is field 4), and AuthoritativeState
requires an explicit entries array. Corrected numeric and child-authority witnesses pass.
## Qualification pass 3 — allocation/source controls and output-closure correction

`campaign2ProbeAllocationFailure.test.ts`: 18 cases PASS. Injection calls the real working
allocator, then throws before its value returns to probe execution. All five advances in each
suppressed branch and the three probe-owned advances in the permitted branch roll back with
clock, queue, state, outputs and trace. The two EVID-owned permitted advances remain covered by
the evaluation/evidence trace-failure cases. Every failed run's checkpoint recovers identically
to an independent clean run. No diagnostic becomes a resumable failed save.

`campaign2ProbeSourceAuthority.test.ts`: public facade has no scheduling/cancellation/allocation
surface. Handler emission of a probe source rejects with INPUT_ONLY_EVENT_ORIGIN_VIOLATION.
Restore rejects removed/duplicated sources, changed time/sequence/parents/definition and changed
original manifest. A valid second opportunity executes and resumes identically. These augment
the existing component admission/reuse/closed-token controls.

`campaign2ProbeIrrelevantState.test.ts`: five public runs hold D=1 fixed and vary each of the
other four valid persistent maps independently. All probe outputs are byte-identical; each full
state remains byte-identical to its own initial state, with exactly the D read recorded.

**Detected implementation defect and correction:** the first `extra-learning` substitution in
`campaign2ProbeOutputClosure.test.ts` unexpectedly committed successfully. The trace adapter used
the first output without enforcing the complete probe output list. A well-formed learning record
could therefore be appended by a substituted host producer outside the EVID route. This was not
a legitimate model option or a shape change, and no qualification PASS was assigned to it.

The corrected trace binding enforces exact per-slot cardinality and record type: available
source emits one 334; permitted observation one 203; permitted freeze one 227; other probe slots
emit none. Extra or replacement learning rejects atomically. Existing ingress rejects raw 203
and truth 334 substituted as a SEM freeze. The archive validator enforces the same producer
matrix and exact ordered equality between saved outputs and trace output projections, rejecting
untraced learning or reassignment of learning to the probe freeze producer. It performs no
historical truth recomputation and introduces no provenance/identity system. All five output
closure tests now PASS; valid original saves remain byte-identical.

Runtime matrices and persistence validation changed only beneath the already frozen contract.
Whole-probe qualification remains open: remaining substitutions must still establish the full
PROBE-B/G/M/O negative surface. The additional evidence above is not an ADAPT-9b or PHEN verdict.
## Remaining work

Whole PROBE-A..P qualification and remaining adversarial controls,
ADAPT-9b, parent control 9, PHEN-ADAPT and Campaign 2 completion remain open. No appraisal,
performance/physiology response, reward, scalar carriage into X/E/L, unit conversion or cognitive
learning was added. Relevant reference-mechanism dispositions remain SUB001 exact arithmetic,
SUB008 trace/rollback, SUB009 paired intervention and SUB011 failure history; SUB012 response
law remains deferred.

Initial test-authoring failures used the wrong compiled-content property and save field 2 for
RunIdentity. Correcting the fixtures to `compiled.content` and field 3 made their positive paths
pass; no production semantics changed to accommodate them. An earlier paired test incorrectly
compared omniscient adaptation outputs as observer projections; its selection was corrected to
the permitted observation/X/E/L records. Build typing corrections did not alter the accepted math.

Pass-3 final verification: **84 files / 549 tests PASS**, production build and reference boundary
PASS. Fresh-process continuation remains the same 55,782-byte complete save and SHA256. Frozen
successor verification reproduces fda39ae4a8d82cbf531b41ce35c9af7ebb2ec5c7f233c4f7adbd7e6d7eba80e9
and preserves all 45 prior packet files. No new review decision was required for these fixes.
## Pass 4 — remaining negative controls and review packaging

Focused public matched-allocation scalar test PASS. Twelve in-memory production substitutions
cover wrong maps/root/C/V, duplicate read and scalar embedding/hash/branch/metadata carriage;
all DETECTED. Four diagnostic numeric substitutions (clipping, saturation, threshold, gain)
are DETECTED in the accepted generic signed domain. Six SEM source substitutions (classification,
dereference, hashing, embedding and metadata) are REJECTED. All reports carry fingerprints and
